supersedes: The 54 body_needed entries in next_body_queue.json now have scientific scope decisions below. Their original abstract reads are reused, not credited again.
source_integrity_note: Two apparent page-count discrepancies were resolved by fresh text extraction and physical-page checks. Text was byte-identical; embedded control characters caused naive page counting errors. No extra reading credit was added.

records.title: ChatR1: Reinforcement Learning for Conversational Reasoning and Retrieval Augmented Question Answering
records.central_contribution: Conversational search/reasoning with turn-level intent rewards.
records.scope_evidence: Actual data/evaluation are open-domain TopicOCQA/QReCC/INSCIT, FaithDial grounding and governmental MultiDoc2Dial; results compare evolving-intent retrieval/generation rather than a medical task.

records.title: TeRA: Vector-based Random Tensor Network for High-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
records.central_contribution: Parameter-efficient high-rank adaptation via frozen tensor factors and learned scaling vectors.
records.scope_evidence: Experiments develop parameter-efficiency/rank claims in Commonsense170k, ConvAI2 persona dialogue and Math10k/AQuA/SVAMP arithmetic. No medically primary research objective or experiment program.

records.title: GenDis: Generative-Discriminative Dual-View Co-Training for Generalized Category Discovery
records.central_contribution: Generalized category discovery using generative/discriminative dual-view co-training.
records.scope_evidence: MCID genuinely concerns COVID-19 service intents, but primary task is open-world known/novel category discovery and experimental axes are known-class/labeled ratios, clustering and co-training across banking, assistants and technical questions. MCID is a generalization test of that program, not medical primacy.

records.title: DE-CLIP: Few-Shot Anomaly Detection via Difference-Guided Embedding Editing
records.central_contribution: Cross-domain, training-free CLIP anomaly detection via textual and visual difference-vector editing.
records.scope_evidence: Medical MRI evidence is substantive (Tables4/6,p.7, localization p.8), but §2.2–3.2 pp.3–4 builds the phenomenon/mechanism on MVTec industrial categories. §4.4 pp.8–9 develops component, hyperparameter, lexicon and semantic-direction evidence on MVTec; §4.5 p.9 calls MRI a transfer from industrial imagery; §4.7 extends the central representation claim to CIFAR-100. Actual primary research is general/industrial visual anomaly representation, with medical corroboration, not a medically primary method.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline industrial and MRI anomaly-detection benchmarks. Excluded by actual primary focus, not method generality or number of medical datasets.

records.title: Mixture-of-Minds: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Table Understanding
records.central_contribution: Planning/coding/answering multi-agent RL for table reasoning.
records.scope_evidence: Healthcare is a motivating application, while actual TableInstruct/TableBench fact-checking/numerical/data-analysis tasks and financial FinQA transfer drive the research and reported results. Not a medical table-study program.

records.title: MMCLIP: Cross-Modal Attention Masked Modelling for Medical Language-Image Pre-Training
records.central_contribution: Medical language-image pretraining using pathology-focused cross-modal image masking and medical-entity text masking, with disease prompts permitting unpaired chest images.
records.scope_evidence: §1 pp.1–2 states the medical data/lesion representation problem; §2 pp.2–6 develops AttMIM/EntMLM with medical report/disease interactions; §3 pp.6–8 tests MIMIC-CXR/PadChest pretraining, chest-X-ray disease classification and medical ablations. All principal evidence concerns medical representation learning.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Retrospective/offline chest-radiograph datasets, zero-shot and fine-tuned classification, not prospective patient-outcome validation.

records.title: MMSearch-R1: Incentivizing LMMs to Search
records.body_sections_read: pp.1–2,4,6; p.7 result narrative partly inspected; §1,2.1–2.2,3.1,4.1–4.2
records.central_contribution: On-demand multimodal search trained with outcome rewards and search penalties.
records.scope_evidence: FactualVQA construction starts from WordNet/Wikipedia visual concepts and mixed image-information needs; experiments measure search use and answer quality on general FVQA/InfoSeek/MMSearch/SimpleVQA/LiveVQA. Neither sampling nor primary result organization establishes a medical focus.

records.title: Toward Secure Tuning: Mitigating Security Risks from Instruction Fine-Tuning
records.central_contribution: Security-preserving instruction fine-tuning using robust-module warm-up.
records.scope_evidence: Medical knowledge appears in broad motivation, but main study trains UltraInteract reasoning/Alpaca, measures security/task tradeoffs across LLMs and attack conditions, and extends to GSM8K. The primary empirical program is generic LLM tuning security, not medical model safety.

records.title: Coordinating Search-Informed Reasoning and Reasoning-Guided Search in Claim Verification
records.central_contribution: Coordinated reasoning/search agents for multi-hop claim verification.
records.scope_evidence: Verification chains, bridging facts and search-agent coordination are evaluated in EX-FEVER/HOVER with Wikipedia retrieval and CHECKWHY generalization. Biomedical validation is not the primary task or analysis.

records.title: PUPPET: Neural-Symbolic Standardized Patients for Mental Health
records.body_sections_read: 1–10 main narrative, with text from figure-heavy p.3 partially truncated; targeted Appendix B.3.2 pp.20–21
records.central_contribution: Neural-symbolic virtual standardized patients and explainable training feedback for mental-health practitioners.
records.scope_evidence: §1 pp.1–2 distinguishes clinical standardized-patient education from generic persona simulation; §3 pp.4–6 defines Observe–Think–Behave/rule-driven patient states and trainee feedback; §4 pp.6–9 evaluates CBT/MI fidelity, hotline simulation and pedagogy. Appendix B.3.2 pp.20–21 specifies the human training protocol.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Simulated patients and largely automatic/expert-rated fidelity, plus a five-week randomized educational study of 30 novice counselors (10/group). Outcome is self-reported confidence using selected CASES-R items, not prospective patient treatment benefit or proven real-clinic therapist competence.

records.title: LightReasoner: Can Small Language Models Teach Large Language Models Reasoning?
records.central_contribution: Expert–amateur token-divergence self-distillation for efficient reasoning.
records.scope_evidence: Operational design, supervised sample generation and main results concern math reasoning (GSM8K and math/STEM benchmarks), accuracy and computational economy, not biomedical experiments.

records.title: SCAN: Structured Capability Assessment and Navigation for LLMs
records.central_contribution: Fine-grained LLM capability taxonomy, query synthesis and judge evaluation.
records.scope_evidence: Actual SCAN benchmark samples writing/roleplay/knowledge/coding/math/reasoning, with model and language-specific capability analyses. Bioengineering weakness is a category-level example within broad capability profiling, not primary biomedical research.

records.title: EMCEE: Improving Multilingual Capability of LLMs via Bridging Knowledge and Reasoning with Extracted Synthetic Multilingual Context
records.central_contribution: Multilingual context elicitation and reasoning-response merging.
records.scope_evidence: Actual design and tests concern language/cultural grounding across exam QA, open-domain MKQA, entailment XNLI and commonsense XCOPA; evaluation axes are high/low-resource languages and prompting. Not medically primary.

records.title: RealTalk-CN: A Realistic Chinese Speech Task-Oriented Dialogue Benchmark with Cross-Modal Analysis
records.central_contribution: Chinese speech/text task-oriented dialogue benchmark with modality-switching and disfluency robustness.
records.scope_evidence: Healthcare is among daily-task domains, but construction seeks broad real-life assistant interactions, scripted/improvised speech and demographic variation; principal experiments are intent/slot/chat accuracy, disfluency and modality effects. Ordinary disfluencies and human speech participants are not a clinical speech-disorder study.

records.title: HOPE: Hybrid Optimized Parallel Encoding with Supervised and Unsupervised Semantic Fusion for Depression Symptom Detection
records.central_contribution: Depressive-symptom ranking/classification by supervised DepRoBERTa and transductive semantic clustering initialized with clinical symptom descriptions, plus learned fusion.
records.scope_evidence: §1 pp.1–2 and §3 pp.3–5 define depression symptom detection as the actual task; §4 pp.5–7 evaluates eRisk, ReDSM5, PRIMATE and DepressionEmo with symptom metrics; §5 pp.8–9 investigates overlapping/missed symptoms and annotation ambiguity. Medical/mental-health specificity is central to design, targets and experiments.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline English Reddit benchmarks, unlabeled-test transductive clustering; human/weak symptom annotations rather than prospectively confirmed diagnoses. Sentence-level limitations and unknown cross-platform/demographic transfer, p.10.

records.title: Bias Fitting to Mitigate Length Bias of Reward Model in RLHF
records.central_contribution: A nonlinear response-length bias fitting model and alternating debiasing framework for RLHF reward models.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, §1: the aim is to characterize nonlinear response-length/reward correlations and improve general preference modeling. Physical p.3, §3: warm-up, bias fitting and debiasing form the method. Physical pp.5–6, §4.1–4.2: Anthropic HH preference data train reward models; DPO and best-of-N are evaluated by Alpaca-Eval length-controlled win rate, MT-Bench conversation performance and IFEval instruction following. Results analyze chosen/rejected response length, rewards and preference quality.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline human-preference datasets and benchmark/judge-based alignment evaluation; no medical deployment or patient outcomes are demonstrated.

records.title: Rethinking Sample Polarity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
records.central_contribution: An analysis of positive/negative RLVR sample polarity and adaptive asymmetric token-level advantage shaping.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, §1: the question concerns exploration, entropy, response length and the differing training roles of correct/incorrect reasoning samples. Physical p.7, §5.1: A3PO dynamically weights token categories then decays the asymmetric weighting. Physical p.8, §5.2–5.4: principal evaluations use AIME24, AIME25, MATH500, GPQA and LiveCodeBench; the main claims concern training stability/generalization and ablations use math benchmarks. Physical p.13, Appendix A: training uses DAPO-Math, verifying that the concrete training program is math-centered.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline benchmark training and evaluation of language-model reasoning, not a biomedical experimental or clinical protocol.

additional_reading_windows_utc.note: Shared supplementary-read batch covering only selected appendix pages of .134/.145/.154/.161; not additional unique paper credit.

records.title: Two-Stage Regularization-Based Structured Pruning for LLMs
records.central_contribution: Two-stage regularization transfers information before layer pruning to reduce LLM size without retraining.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: efficient LLM deployment and pruning-induced knowledge loss motivate the study. Physical p.3, §3: layer weights are learned and low-weight layers regularized before removal, with data from Alpaca/WikiText-2/PTB/C4. Physical pp.5–6, §4 and Table 1: perplexity on WikiText-2, accuracy on PIQA/WinoGrande/HellaSwag/ARC and latency/throughput are the central outcomes; pruning ratios and calibration-dataset dependence are tested.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline model-compression experiments and hardware measurements on general corpora.

records.title: K-Merge: Online Continual Merging of Adapters for On-device Large Language Models
records.central_contribution: Data-free similarity clustering and history-aware merging of incrementally arriving LoRA adapters under a limited on-device storage budget.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1,3, §1/§3: the application is adding generative language capabilities to mobile devices under storage/compute limits. Physical pp.4–5, §4: K-Merge clusters similar adapters and performs running-average merges with history tracking. Physical pp.6–7, §5.1–5.2: 40 task/language combinations cover smart reply (Persona-Chat), summarization (SAMSum), tone adjustment, SQuAD QA and grammar correction; results compare normalized task performance and robustness to task order under varying storage budgets.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Simulated sequential adapter arrival, offline task datasets, and assumed perfect task identification (§3.3); this is not a medical deployment study.

records.title: CiPO: Counterfactual Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models through Iterative Preference Optimization
records.central_contribution: Counterfactual answer/reasoning generation with iterative preference optimization to forget targeted facts while preserving model utility.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: privacy/copyright information removal and leakage through reasoning traces motivate the work. Physical p.6, §4.2: the method pairs counterfactual desired outputs with newly sampled undesired outputs. Physical pp.7–8, §5.1–5.2 and Tables 1–3: R-TOFU uses fictitious biographical QA and reasoning traces; the real-world RETURN evaluation selects 260 QA pairs about public figures, splitting forget/retain sets. Outcomes are answer/reasoning forgetting, utility and general GSM8K/MMLU/WikiText preservation.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline synthetic and model-memorized QA evaluations; real-world here describes biographical data, not clinical deployment.

records.title: DIA-HARM: Dialectal Disparities in Harmful Content Detection Across 50 English Dialects
records.central_contribution: A corpus and evaluation framework for disinformation-detection robustness across 50 English dialects.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, §1: four principal questions ask about unseen dialects, dialect-aware training, cross-dialect transfer and detector architecture. Physical p.4, §3–4 and Table 1: rule-based dialect transformations preserve semantic content/labels; sources deliberately cover political misinformation, health misinformation (CoAID/MM-COVID), social-media rumors, multilingual claims and AI-generated content. Physical pp.6–8, §5–6: comparisons are organized by dialect, human/AI/mixed content, exposure regime and architecture; main results and errors concern language-variation robustness.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline rule-transformed text corpus and classifier/LLM evaluation; semantic/label preservation and dialect authenticity are evaluation issues, not prospective health-impact evidence.

records.title: Towards Scalable Lifelong Knowledge Editing with Selective Knowledge Suppression
records.central_contribution: LightEdit uses a relevance selector and suppression of original answer probabilities to make scalable nonparametric lifelong knowledge edits.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: continual fact updates, catastrophic forgetting and editing costs define the problem. Physical pp.4–5, §4: relevant retrieved edited facts are selected and original first-token knowledge probabilities downweighted. Physical pp.5–7, §5 and Table 1: 1,000 sequential edits on ZSRE/Counterfact/RIPE are assessed for reliability, generality, locality and scaling. Physical p.13, Appendix B: general capability checks cover commonsense, multi-domain MMLU, ANLI and open-domain TriviaQA; the worked edit example is a political office fact.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline sequential fact-edit benchmarks and general-capability evaluation, not validated medical-knowledge maintenance.

additional_reading_windows_utc.note: Shared supplementary-read batch covering only selected appendix pages of .134/.145/.154/.161; not additional unique paper credit.

records.title: Optimizing Length Compression in Large Reasoning Models
records.central_contribution: LC-R1 compresses unnecessary post-answer reasoning using valid-segment extraction and complementary length/compression rewards.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1,3, §1–2: overthinking is quantified by valid-thinking rates across math benchmarks. Physical p.4, §3/Figure 3: a parser extracts valid thinking, dual rewards guide GRPO, and essential steps are retained. Physical p.6, §4.1: training mixes AIME/MATH; evaluation covers five math benchmarks plus GPQA-Diamond and LiveCodeBench. Physical p.7, Table 2/§4.3: the primary trade-off is token reduction versus reasoning accuracy; science/coding are explicitly OOD checks.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline benchmark training/evaluation with answer extraction; no biomedical outcome validation.

records.title: Evolutionary Guided Decoding: Iterative Value Refinement for LLMs
records.central_contribution: Iterative Value Refinement improves value-guided decoding by combining multi-trajectory exploration with self-refinement.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: the target is distribution mismatch in decoding-time general alignment. Physical p.4, §3: current-policy trajectories are scored and the value function repeatedly refined. Physical pp.5–7, §4.1–4.3: Reddit TL;DR summarization, Anthropic HH dialogue and UltraFeedback/Alpaca-Eval instruction following drive the experiments. Results compare reward/KL trade-offs, judge win rates and compute; component analyses use multi-turn dialogue.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline preference corpora with learned rewards and LLM-judge checks; reward/judge metrics are not biomedical outcomes.

records.title: COMPASS: Enhancing Agent Long-Horizon Reasoning with Evolving Context
records.central_contribution: COMPASS separates a main tool-using agent, strategic meta-thinker and context manager to maintain coherent long-horizon reasoning.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: the problem is error accumulation in long multi-tool tasks, illustrated by a sports lookup. Physical pp.3–5, §3: tactical execution, monitoring and context refresh form the framework. Physical p.5, §4: evaluation uses non-image GAIA, BrowseComp web tasks and HLE questions spanning mathematics, humanities and natural sciences. Physical p.6, §4.1: main claims and BrowseComp ablations concern persistence, pivoting, recovery, termination and token efficiency.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Benchmark tool-using agent evaluation and LLM-judged trajectory metrics; not prospective clinical/scientific use validation.

records.title: BracketRank: Large Language Model Document Ranking via Reasoning-based Competitive Elimination
records.central_contribution: Reasoning-enhanced bracket competition and adaptive grouping for zero-shot document reranking.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: reasoning-intensive retrieval and context/order limitations motivate the work. Physical pp.3,5, §3: documents compete in winner/loser bracket groups to form a ranking. Physical pp.5–6, §4/Table 2–4: the primary program spans BRIGHT scientific/economic/coding/math domains and TREC, BEIR and NovelEval. Biology in BRIGHT and Covid/NFCorpus/SciFact in BEIR are substantive biomedical-bearing evaluations. Physical p.7, §4.2–5.2: the paper emphasizes broad ranking gains and uses TREC DL19 for reasoning ablation and cross-model robustness.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline zero-shot reranking of pre-retrieved candidates, evaluated with relevance metrics; no biomedical decision or patient-impact study.

records.title: Multi-component Causal Tracing in Large Language Models
records.body_sections_read: §1; intervention formulation; optimization method; §5.1–5.2; Appendix C.2
records.central_contribution: Penalized gradient-based simultaneous selection of influential LLM attention heads/MLP units for causal tracing.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: the research objective is LLM interpretability, bias and knowledge flow. Physical pp.4,6: counterfactual activation interventions and a transformed metric with sparse/binary regularization define the method. Physical pp.7–8, §5/Tables/Figure 3: attention-head experiments use WinoGender/WinoBias; MLP experiments use Professions and CounterFact, optimizing bias/factuality metrics and execution time. Physical pp.13–14, Appendix C.2/Table 3: data are occupational-pronoun stereotypes, ordinary world facts and arithmetic variable-binding prompts.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline intervention tests on selected language prompts; causal attribution inside a model is not biological/clinical causality.

additional_reading_windows_utc.note: Shared supplementary-read batch covering only selected appendix pages of .134/.145/.154/.161; not additional unique paper credit.

records.title: TensorLens: End-to-End Transformer Analysis via High-Order Attention Tensors
records.central_contribution: A high-order tensor formulation of an entire Transformer as an input-dependent linear operator for model analysis.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1 and p.3, §3: the goal and construction concern global attention/FFN/normalization/residual interactions inside Transformers. Physical pp.6–8, §4: perturbation tests evaluate DeiT on ImageNet-1K, BERT-family models on IMDB and decoder models on WikiText-103. Relation decoding probes ordinary bias, commonsense and factual relations, such as occupation/workplace mappings, as approximations of model computation.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline attribution/perturbation and relation-decoding proxy tests; no biomedical validation or clinical protocol.

records.title: OASIS: Online Sample Selection for Continual Instruction Tuning
records.central_contribution: OASIS adaptively samples informative and nonredundant examples for online continual instruction tuning.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1 and p.3, §3: real-time learning under shifting instruction streams is the aim; informativeness statistics and redundancy elimination define the method. Physical pp.5–7, §4: principal comparisons vary sample-selection ratio and computation budget, centered on the proposed MICVIT multi-image stream, with broader text/multimodal CIT transfer. Physical p.16, Appendix A.4: MICVIT includes natural-image reasoning, chart and image-edit/pattern datasets; COAST-domain contains DocVQA/ChartQA/IconQA/MedicalQA, while text streams include general NLU, sentiment, code and mathematical reasoning.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline datasets arranged into simulated continual streams; the appendix assumes infinite episodic memory. No prospective clinical adaptation or patient outcomes.

records.title: Mitigating Context Interference for Reliable and Efficient Search Agents
records.central_contribution: Context refinement distillation and context-refined RL to reduce distracting retrieved text in multi-turn search agents.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: reliability/efficiency losses from irrelevant retrieved documents motivate the work. Physical p.3, §3.1: search uses a Wikipedia dump and general single-hop/multi-hop QA (NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle). Physical pp.5,7, §3.3/§4.1: a distilled refiner extracts query-relevant evidence and is integrated into RL rollouts. Physical p.8, §4.2–4.3/Tables 3–4: training uses NQ/HotpotQA and main outcomes are QA exact match, retrieval counts, context length and latency.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline QA benchmarks with fixed retrieval corpus and trained search-agent evaluation; no medical deployment validation.

records.title: Chunks as Arms: Multi-Armed Bandit-Guided Sampling for Long-Context LLM Preference Optimization
records.central_contribution: Multi-armed-bandit selection of context chunks generates useful diverse preference pairs for long-context DPO.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: lost-in-the-middle and synthetic preference-data quality motivate the study. Physical pp.3–5, §3: chunks are arms, rewards score answers, and UCB/probe initialization manage exploration. Physical pp.5–7, §4–5: MuSiQue training is lengthened with random Wikipedia documents; evaluation and ablations use multi-hop/general-field/narrative long-context QA, with substring exact match and F1. Physical p.12, Appendix A.4 lists the five test sets and their lengths/sizes.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline synthetic preference construction, artificially lengthened contexts and benchmark QA evaluation; no medical validation.

additional_reading_windows_utc.note: Shared supplementary-read batch covering only selected appendix pages of .134/.145/.154/.161; not additional unique paper credit.

records.title: Long Context Modeling with Ranked Memory-Augmented Retrieval
records.central_contribution: ERMAR ranks memory key-value entries and adaptively retrieves/prunes them for long-context language modeling.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: customer-support dialogue and long-context memory motivate the framework. Physical pp.3–5, §3: semantic retrieval and relevance reranking select memory entries; the training target remains next-token prediction. Physical p.5, §3.1: SlimPajama fine-tuning, WikiText-103/PG19/Proof-Pile evaluation and sentiment/subjectivity/opinion tasks define the concrete application. Physical pp.6–7, §3.2/Tables 1–4: outcomes are perplexity, in-context task accuracy and GPU memory efficiency.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline corpus evaluation across context lengths and hardware metrics; no biomedical deployment or clinical outcomes.

records.title: Debiased Orthogonal Boundary-Driven Efficient Noise Mitigation
records.central_contribution: One-Step Anti-noise uses an external multimodal estimator and a debiased orthogonal boundary to reweight noisy training samples.
records.scope_evidence: Physical p.1, §1: label-noise robustness across cross-modal matching, image classification and image retrieval is the aim. Physical pp.5–6, §3.2: shared-space estimator similarities become cleanliness weights for the target-model loss. Physical pp.6–7, §4.2–4.4: MSCOCO/Flickr30K/CC120K/CC3M image-text matching, WebFG Aircraft/Bird/Car classification and CARS98N retrieval form the actual experiments. Physical p.13, Appendix A confirms the generic image/caption and vehicle/animal image datasets and simulated/real noisy-label protocols.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline visual benchmarks with injected and web-collected label noise. Extracted pp.2/5 contain noisy embedded legacy-figure text; the clean §4/Appendix A evidence and official collection/footer, not that artifact, determine scope and formal type.

records.title: Collaborative Chain-of-Agents for Parametric-Retrieved Knowledge Synergy
records.central_contribution: CoCoA combines internal parametric knowledge and externally retrieved evidence through collaborating reasoning agents.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, §1: The problem and contributions are open-domain question answering and synergy between parametric and retrieved knowledge. Physical pp.3, 5, §3.1–3.2; §4.1–4.2: Internal and external agents contribute reasoning; training and evaluation use HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, WebQuestions and TriviaQA with a Wikipedia retrieval corpus. Physical pp.6, 8, Table 1; §4.4, §4.9–4.10; §5: Main results compare QA exact-match/F1 and agent ablations. Non-QA transfer and passage-count robustness broaden the general retrieval argument.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline QA and retrieval benchmarks, with answer-quality and robustness metrics; not a clinical study.

records.title: Compressing then Matching: An Efficient Pre-training Paradigm for Multimodal Embedding
records.central_contribution: CoMa pre-trains multimodal embeddings by compressing representations before cross-modal matching.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, §1; §3.1: The target is broadly useful multimodal embeddings rather than biomedical image-text representations; contrastive embedding learning supplies the method context. Physical pp.5, §3.2.3–3.3; §4.1; Table 1: Compression/masking and generated image dialogue support pre-training. Listed pre-training sources include CIRR, HatefulMemes, MSCOCO, N24News, SUN397, VOC2007, Visual7W and WebQA. Physical pp.6, 12, Table 2; §4.3–5; Table 4: MMEB-V1 results cover classification, VQA, retrieval and grounding with in-/out-of-distribution splits; the complete dataset table confirms natural-image, news, document, chart and related broad tasks.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline multimodal embedding benchmark evaluation with retrieval/classification-style metrics.

records.title: LLM-XTM: Enhancing Cross-Lingual Topic Models with Large Language Models
records.central_contribution: LLM-XTM uses LLM-based topic-word refinement, self-consistency and semantic matching to improve cross-lingual topic modeling.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, §1: The stated goal is cross-lingual topic coherence and alignment, not biomedical topic discovery. Physical pp.3–4, §3: Topic-word refinement and document-semantic matching are the operative learning components. Physical pp.6–7, §4; Table 2; §4.3–4.4: Actual corpora are EC News in English/Chinese, Amazon English/Chinese product reviews, and Rakuten-Amazon Japanese/English reviews. Results and ablations assess topic coherence, uniqueness and quality.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline multilingual topic-model experiments and model-based topic-quality evaluation.

records.title: SAGE: Sparse Adaptive Guidance for Dependency-Aware Tabular Data Generation
records.central_contribution: SAGE provides sparse, dependency-aware guidance for autoregressive tabular-data generation using selected feature dependencies and logit correction.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, 4, §1; §3.1–3.3: The motivating objective is general tabular synthesis with dependencies and constraints across application sectors; the method selects informative pseudo-feature dependencies to guide generated rows. Physical pp.6, §4.1–4.2: There are real biomedical datasets: MIC biological/hospitalization variables and CDC Diabetes. The same core protocol includes Adult Income, HELOC, Iris and California Housing and measures synthetic-to-real task utility, realism and privacy. Physical pp.7–9, Table 1; §5; Figures 3–4; §6: Main evidence is cross-domain task utility and controllable distributional fidelity. Adult consistency and Housing geographic/policy constraints receive focused analyses, and the conclusion foregrounds Adult/Housing gains rather than a medical objective.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline tabular synthesis and downstream predictive utility on held-out real data; no prospective clinical workflow or patient benefit is established.

records.title: Mask-to-Correct+: Leveraging Retriever Diversity for Masking-guided Faithful Fact Correction
records.central_contribution: Mask-to-Correct+ combines diverse retrievers and masking-guided correction to improve faithful fact correction without gold evidence.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–4, §1; Figure 2; §3: The paper targets generic factual-error correction and introduces retriever-diverse masking, evidence-based correction and scoring/ensemble selection. A pulmonary-embolism example is genuinely medical. Physical pp.4–6, §4.1–4.2; Tables 1–2: Both FEVER (general/Wikipedia) and SciFact (scientific claims with S2ORC retrieval) are evaluated. SciFact supplies substantial biomedical/scientific claim content, rather than just a title-level mention. Physical pp.7–9, 15, §5.1–5.3; Tables 4–5; appendix validation details: The experimental program tests masking, faithfulness and retrieval diversity. FEVER anchors validation, retriever-combination and compute analyses; SciFact is a separate scientific transfer/evaluation arm. The conclusion is generalized faithful fact correction.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline fact-correction benchmarks with retrieved evidence and automated scoring; not deployed clinical fact checking.

records.title: UniversalRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Corpora of Diverse Modalities and Granularities
records.central_contribution: UniversalRAG routes queries across sources with different modalities and granularities, including a no-retrieval option.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, §1; §2.2: The problem is general multimodal/multigranularity retrieval rather than a medical information pathway; routing separates modality-specific corpora. Physical pp.4, §3.1: Actual tasks include MMLU without retrieval, NQ/HotpotQA text, HybridQA tables, MRAG-Bench/WebQA/InfoSeek images and LVBench/VideoRAG video sources. Physical pp.5, Table 1; §3.2: Main results compare source/modality configurations across those broad QA benchmarks.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline multimodal QA benchmark comparisons; no clinical deployment.

records.title: Crossing the Reward Bridge: Expanding Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Across Diverse Domains
records.central_contribution: The paper extends reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to diverse non-mathematical domains through learned soft rewards.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, §1–2; §3.1; Figure 2: The explicit goal is expansion across diverse disciplines. ExamQA contains college subjects including medicine, pharmacy and biology alongside many nonmedical disciplines; no biomedical-focused selection is specified. Physical pp.4–5, Main evaluation protocol; Tables 1–2: Main results are organized into broad STEM, social-science, humanities and applied subject groups. Out-of-distribution evaluation uses mathematical and general knowledge/reasoning benchmarks. Physical pp.6, §4.2: Additional free-form data experiments test cross-domain reward-model transfer rather than a medical decision pathway.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline exam/question-answering and reward-model benchmark evaluation; medical-exam accuracy is not clinical efficacy.

records.title: From ID to LLM: Rethinking Representation Learning for Recommendation
records.central_contribution: Profile-then-Embed converts collaborative recommendation signals into user/item profiles and learns discriminative embeddings.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, 4, §1; §4: The target is ID-versus-LLM representation learning for recommendation; the method creates bidirectional user/item profiles and optimizes their distinctiveness. Physical pp.5–6, §5.1–5.3; Table 2: Main data are Amazon Movies, Toys and Sports with Yelp, Fashion and Beauty tests. Evaluation uses chronological/leave-one-out and cold-start recommendation protocols. Physical pp.7, Tables 3–4: Results analyze cold-start and long-tail recommendation quality on those commerce/media sources.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline historical user-item recommendation with ranking metrics; no medical study.

records.title: DMHM: Density-aware Manifold Learning and Hybrid Mahalanobis Energy for LLMs-generated Text Detection
records.central_contribution: DMHM detects LLM-generated text using density-aware manifold representations and hybrid Mahalanobis energy.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, 6, §1; §3; §4.1: The objective is robust generated-text detection across domains, generators and attacks. Main corpora are Deepfake, M4 and RAID. Physical pp.7–8, Table 1; §4.2, §4.4–4.5: Main classification results use AUROC/accuracy/FPR95 with unseen-generator/domain and attack analyses. Physical pp.12, 15, Appendix A.1; Tables 6–8: PubMed technical QA appears in an unseen-LLM comparison alongside general text sources. Dataset tables show broad reviews, news, stories, online discussion, QA, scientific/general documents and code.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline binary text-source classification, transfer and attack robustness; no clinical outcome evaluation.

records.title: Can We Predict Before Executing Machine Learning Agents?
records.central_contribution: The paper predicts relative ML-agent solution quality before execution and applies the predictor in FOREAGENT to reduce search execution cost.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–5, §1; §3.1–3.4; §4–5; Table 2: The central contribution is an execution-free preference predictor and an 18,438-pair corpus spanning 26 tasks across computer vision, NLP and data science. Main tests assess pairwise prediction accuracy and generalization over ML tasks/algorithms/difficulty, not a biomedical endpoint. Physical pp.8, §6.2–6.4: The FOREAGENT application includes genuine biomedical-bearing tasks: Stanford COVID Vaccine/mRNA degradation prediction, ventilator pressure, and histopathology cancer classification, alongside iceberg and cactus tasks. These are high-level application identities only. Physical pp.15–19, Appendix B; Table 6: The documented task selection tests scientific-domain generalization and search efficiency; corpus/task details extend across broad vision, NLP and data-science problems, also including a retinopathy task. Biomedical content is substantial but embedded within a deliberately cross-domain ML-agent study.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline/budgeted ML-agent benchmark runs and solution-ranking evaluation. Biomedical benchmark scores do not demonstrate prospective clinical benefit or wet-lab validation. Biological details were kept at high-level scope only.

records.title: IMPACT: Importance-Aware Activation Space Reconstruction
records.central_contribution: IMPACT compresses LLMs through importance-aware activation-space reconstruction.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, 5, §1; §3; §3.6–3.7: The method reconstructs compressed activations with loss/gradient-derived importance and eigenvector-based profiling. Physical pp.6, §4.1: Actual task families are mathematical reasoning and code generation. Calibration data are MetaMathQA and CodeInstructions; tests include GSM8K, MATH, MBPP and HumanEval. Physical pp.7, §4.2–4.3: Main results compare model size/compression with task performance and Pass@1 rather than a medical task.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline model-compression benchmarks and task accuracy; no medical deployment.

records.title: Looking at Radiology Report Generation through a Causal Lens: A Survey
records.central_contribution: Medical radiology-report generation survey organizing pipeline bias, causal modeling and data/model/evaluation interventions.
records.scope_evidence: §1 pp.1–2 establishes RRG-specific aim; §2–4 pp.2–8 analyze medical reporting/data/LLM biases, structural causal modeling and mitigation taxonomy; §5 pp.8–9 examines medical imaging datasets and report metrics; §6 and Limitations pp.9–10 retain the clinical RRG focus.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Survey/conceptual synthesis, not a new experimental intervention. §4 p.8 and Limitations p.10 explicitly state no experimental evaluation of mitigation methods; prospective validation remains a need, not an achieved result.

records.title: CTTA-T: Continual Test-Time Adaptation for Text Understanding via Teacher-Student with a Domain-aware and Generalized Teacher
records.central_contribution: CTTA-T adapts text models continuously under domain shifts using a domain-aware, generalized teacher-student framework.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, §1; §3.1–3.2: The aim is continual text-domain adaptation; motivating shifts include movie/restaurant/book reviews. Teacher filtering/refinement and adaptation mechanisms address general language robustness. Physical pp.6–7, §4.1: The actual sequence includes QA shifts involving noise, reading/search/trivia and cross-lingual tasks, plus sentiment data from movie, restaurant, hotel/travel and other reviews. Physical pp.7, Tables 1 and 3: Main results use sequential QA EM/F1 and multilingual/review sentiment performance, not clinical language outcomes.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline sequential test-time adaptation and benchmark evaluation, not a prospective clinical system.

records.title: Disco-RAG: Discourse-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.central_contribution: Disco-RAG models intra-chunk rhetorical structure and inter-chunk discourse relations to plan more coherent retrieval-augmented answers.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–4, §1; §3: The vitamin-D/influenza illustration is medical, but the stated problem is missing discourse structure in general RAG. The method combines intra-chunk RST, an inter-chunk relation graph and discourse planning. Physical pp.4–5, 7, §4–5; Tables 2–3: Main evaluations are Loong knowledge-intensive tasks, ASQA long-form QA and SciNews scientific lay summarization. The principal categories are locating/comparison/clustering/chain reasoning, answer quality and summarization quality. Physical pp.8–9, 17, Tables 4–5; human-evaluation discussion; Appendix C: Module/planning ablations and mixed-model checks mainly use Loong, with scientific-summary coherence/faithfulness judged separately. Parser checks use RST-DT and random examples from each benchmark, not a medically focused protocol.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline QA/summarization benchmarks, model-based metrics and human quality judgments; not patient-level or clinical deployment evaluation.

records.title: Controlling Multimodal Conversational Agents with Coverage-Enhanced Latent Actions
records.central_contribution: Coverage-enhanced latent actions provide control over multimodal conversational agents through codebook/action representations and a language world model.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, §1; §3: The intended settings include entertainment, education and personal assistants. The method uses cross-modal representations, latent-action learning and a conversational policy rather than a clinical intervention. Physical pp.5, §4.1: Training uses Conceptual12M, N24News, WikiWeb2M and SlimPajama. Evaluation tasks are multimodal role-playing and personalized conversation through MMRole and PCogAlignBench. Physical pp.6–7, §4.2; Table 1: Metrics assess persona/tone coherence, role awareness, behavior and contextual/mental-state alignment. These conversational dimensions are not clinical or neurobiological measurements.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline dialogue benchmarks and quality/alignment judging; no therapeutic efficacy or clinical validation.

records.title: Guaranteeing Knowledge Integration with Joint Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
records.central_contribution: Contrastive preference learning and joint decoding reconcile internal and externally retrieved knowledge in RAG.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–4, §1; §3: The target is general knowledge integration/conflict. Dual internal/reference answer paths and gated joint decoding implement the solution. Physical pp.4–5, §4.1: The main evaluation uses NQ, TruthfulQA, Wizard of Wikipedia, HotpotQA and ELI5. Physical pp.5–6, §4.2–4.3; Table 1: Results examine QA quality, hallucination/entity precision/coherence, with HotpotQA-focused ablations; no medically focused evaluation program is specified.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline QA/dialogue benchmarks and answer-quality metrics, not clinical deployment.

records.title: Are We Using the Right Benchmark: An Evaluation Framework for Visual Token Compression Methods
records.central_contribution: VTCBench constructs a difficulty-sensitive evaluation framework for visual token compression and tests misleading performance from easier benchmarks.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–4, §1; Table 1; §3.2–3.3: The aim is fair general visual-token compression evaluation. The sources are GQA, MMBench English/Chinese, MME, POPE, MMStar, OCRBench and ChartQA; downsampling/compression behavior differs across general and OCR/chart tasks. Physical pp.6–7, Difficulty selection; §4.1: Hard-example filtering and compression-ratio comparisons construct VTCBench from the same general visual benchmark family. Physical pp.7–8, §4.2; Tables 3–4: Main Qwen2-VL/LLaVA-OneVision comparisons concern natural-image, text-in-image and chart understanding, not medical imaging.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline visual-language benchmark analysis and compression comparisons; not a medical imaging study.

records.title: Retrieval as Generation: A Unified Framework with Self-Triggered Information Planning
records.central_contribution: GRIP treats retrieval as generation with self-triggered information planning and control tokens for retrieval and answering.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–3, §1; method and structured supervision: The contribution is unified general retrieval/answer generation and multihop retrieval-control decisions. Physical pp.5–6, §3.1–3.2; Table 1: Five main open-domain QA datasets are HotpotQA, PopQA, NQ, WebQuestions and TriviaQA. Training uses TriviaQA/NQ; controlled main comparisons use Wikipedia/BM25 retrieval. Physical pp.13, Appendices A–B; Table 10: BioASQ is explicitly added as a domain-specific biomedical transfer evaluation and excluded from the main average. Its medical QA result is real, not merely a mention.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline QA and biomedical transfer benchmark evaluation; no prospective clinical validation.

records.title: EventWeave: A Dynamic Framework for Capturing Core and Supporting Events in Dialogue Systems
records.central_contribution: EventWeave maintains core and supporting events in dynamic graphs for long-context conversation.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–2, §1: The motivating task is maintaining event coherence in general multi-session dialogue, illustrated by personal/festival conversations. Physical pp.3–5, §3–4: The method detects events and temporal/sequential/reasoning relations, builds hierarchical memory graphs and retrieves conversational context; DailyDialog/OpenDialKG support event detection. Physical pp.5–6, §5.1–5.2; Table 1: Chronicle, MSC and LoCoMo test long/multi-session personal dialogue. Outcomes include generation-quality and event-awareness/coverage/coherence measures.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline multi-session dialogue evaluation and model-based quality judging; no therapeutic or clinical evidence.

records.title: Deliberative Searcher: Improving LLM Reliability via Reinforcement Learning with Constraints
records.central_contribution: Deliberative Searcher trains reliable retrieval decisions through constrained reinforcement learning and certainty estimation.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–4, §1–2: The objective is general search correctness and calibration/false certainty; the method constrains a retrieval-using agent rather than optimizing a medical outcome. Physical pp.5, §3.1: Training/evaluation use HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and MuSiQue with Wikipedia retrieval; out-of-domain text-only tests use GAIA and xbench-deepsearch with web search. Physical pp.6, Table 1; §3.4: Main results assess accuracy, reliability, false certainty and test-time compute across these general search/QA tasks.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline benchmarks plus task-based web-search evaluation by the authors; no clinical workflow validation. No searches or paper experiments were reproduced here.

records.title: Thermometer of Thoughts: Enhancing LLM’s Exploration via Attention Temperature Modulation
records.central_contribution: Thermometer of Thoughts modulates attention temperature to improve LLM reasoning exploration.
records.scope_evidence: Physical pp.1–4, §1; §3–4: The target is reasoning exploration through attention/entropy modulation. Cognitive analogies do not constitute brain, EEG or clinical measurements. Physical pp.4–6, §4.1–4.2; §5; Table 1: Mechanism and difficulty analyses use MATH500. The main evaluation explicitly focuses on mathematical reasoning: GSM8K, MATH500, AIME 2024/2025 and HMMT, with additional GPQA and HumanEval tests. Physical pp.7, Table 2: Difficulty-weighted voting is compared on mathematics and generic science reasoning; it does not define a biomedical evaluation program.
records.evidence_protocol_limitations: Offline reasoning/code benchmark scores and model mechanism analysis; no neurobiological or clinical experiment.
